resources.string: Lets Tap Macro show its floating record/play buttons over other apps and replay the taps you record. It cannot read what is on your screen and does not collect or send any data.
Record your taps once, then let your phone replay them on a loop.
Android only lets apps tap the screen for you through Accessibility. Open the settings, tap \"Tap Macro\" (it may be under \"Downloaded apps\" or \"Installed apps\") and switch it on.
Switch greyed out or it says \"Restricted setting\"? Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top corner, choose \"Allow restricted settings\", then try again.

Tap the button below, then open your game. A small floating bar appears:

● Record: play normally, your taps and swipes are recorded (and still go through to the game). Tap ■ to stop and save.
▶ Play: replays the selected macro until you tap ■.
✕ Hides the bar. Drag the dots at the top to move it out of the way.
Floating controls are on screen. Now open your game.
Turn on Tap Macro in Accessibility settings first.
Send taps to the game while recording
Turn this off if you only want to mark where to tap without the game reacting yet.
Nothing recorded yet. Show the floating controls and tap ● to record your first macro.

Tips: keep the floating bar away from spots you tap, because a tap that lands on the bar will not reach the game. Record and play with your phone held the same way (portrait or landscape). If playback stops after a while, turn off battery optimisation for Tap Macro.
● REC: tap ■ on the bar to stop
Nothing recorded, no taps were made.
No macro yet. Tap ● to record one first.
This macro was recorded in %1$s. Turn your phone the same way or the taps will land in the wrong spots.
